newsitem.title: USA: Textron gets $800 million for Paul Revere sale.
newsitem.headline: Textron gets $800 million for Paul Revere sale.

text.p: Textron, Inc., the $9.3 billion multi-industry giant based in Providence, R.I., got out of the insurance business when it announced the completed sale of Paul Revere Corp..

"It was not a great return on investment," Textron Chief Financial Officer Stephen Key said in a telephone interview. "And that's one of the reasons we chose to sell Paul Revere. It's better owned by another insurance company."
Textron said Friday it completed the sale of Paul Revere, a disability insurance company, to The Provident Cos for $20 per share in cash, or $750 million, and $6 per share in Provident common stock.
Textron expects net proceeds of about $800 million after adjustments and contingent payments. It said it intends to use the funds to buy back stock and pay down its debt.
Paul Revere closed at $42.75 on the New York Exchange Thursday. Provident closed at $56 and Textron closed at $103.125, down $3, also on the NYSE.
Key said Textron originally acquired Paul Revere as part of its AVCO purchase in 1985. At the time, the cost was $500 million, he said.

"So the gain is basically the dividends running about $10 million a year and plus proceeds of $800 million from the sale. It's not a great return on investment. That's below our return rates that we consider to be acceptable," Key said.
At the time the deal was announced in April 1996, Paul Revere's stock was trading at about $25, Key said.
